newsitem.title: GERMANY: German prosecutors deny they plan Iran probe.
newsitem.headline: German prosecutors deny they plan Iran probe.

text.p: German prosecutors denied on Wednesday they had decided to lauch a criminal probe into Iran's foreign minister, saying they were still considering whether to investigate Iranian officials "at all levels".

A spokeswoman for the Federal Prosecutor's Office said officials were studying last week's verdict by a German court that top Iranian leaders had ordered the 1992 killing of four Kurdish dissidents. But she said the office had not yet come to a decision.

The Frankfurter Allgeimeine Zeitung newspaper reported in its Wednesday edition that the prosecutor's office had decided to launch a criminal investigation into Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati.
"That's not true," the spokeswoman said, stressing the question was still open.
She said officials were checking whether there were grounds for investigation against Iranian suspects "at all levels". A decision was unlikely to be reached this week, she said.
She said the checks would include whether some suspects were immune from investigation on political or diplomatic grounds.
The Frankfurter Allgemeine said prosecutors had ruled out proceedings against Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei because of "immunity problems".

Last Thursday's verdict marked the first time a European court had clearly attributed political responsibility for any of the dozens of assassinations of Iranian opposition figures abroad since the Islamic revolution in 1979.

The court said Iranian leaders including the state president and the religious leader had ordered the killing. But it only mentioned Intelligence Minister Ali Fallahiyan by name. Iran has denied any involvement.
